case_scope: United States subsystem stress case for refundable credits, benefit delivery, bank/account rails, fee leakage, and paperwork churn

claim_conversion_friction.note: Refundable credits and safety-net programs have large value but incomplete take-up and paperwork interruption block comfort certification.

benefit_take_up_gap.note: EITC participation is materially below 100%; national payment scale cannot be counted as full eligibility conversion.

bank_account_payment_rail_access.note: Unbanked and underbanked households remain a conversion-rail risk even after improvements.

intermediation_fee_leakage.note: Overdraft/NSF and nonbank transaction channels can drain small claims.

auto_enrollment_and_renewal_stability.note: Renewal and paperwork burden can interrupt benefits.

offline_multichannel_access.note: Needs direct evidence on assisted, offline, language, disability, and no-wrong-door routes across programs.

appeal_and_error_correction_access.note: Needs cross-program evidence on identity errors, fraud flags, appeals, and timing.

offset_clawback_or_seizure_risk.note: Need a unified view of offsets, garnishment, clawbacks, overpayments, and account seizure effects.

proof_debt: net usable value after paid filing fees offsets account fees and delays
program-by-program subgroup take-up and denial data
benefit interruption and appeal timing by race disability language rurality and banking status
share of transfers in safe low-cost person-controlled accounts

opening_package.second_lane: safe low-cost account/payment rails and fee protection
opening_package.rail_lane: benefit/tax/identity/appeal data integration with privacy safeguards
opening_package.monitoring_lane: take-up, interruption, fees, delays, appeals, and subgroup conversion gaps

reopening_triggers: EITC or major credit participation changes by more than five points
overdraft/NSF or paid-filing costs rise for low-income claimants
new public filing or benefit-delivery infrastructure is expanded or removed

floor_reality.why: Major claims exist but conversion friction and fee leakage prevent a clean real-floor pass.

washout.why: Fees, delays, and intermediaries can absorb small claims.

conversion_rails.why: Take-up, banking, renewal, fee, and appeal evidence is too weak for comfort certification.

evidence_debt_register.question: What is the net usable value of refundable credits after paid filing, offsets, delays, and bank fees?
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: IRS, CFPB, bank, and household data linked by income and subgroup

evidence_debt_register.question: Which groups experience benefit interruption from paperwork churn?
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: program-by-program churn and recertification data by subgroup

validation_notes: Subsystem case; does not replace the full United States wealth-order case.
